items.title: UWM Removes Minimum Credit Scores on Most Mortgages
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: The nation’s largest mortgage lender just got rid of its minimum credit score requirement on most home loans. The move is effective immediately and applies to conventional loans backed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, as well as FHA, VA, and USDA loans. items.title: Mortgage Rate Relief Lasts All of One Day
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: Well that didn’t take long. One day after mortgage rates finally caught a much-needed break, bond yields are right back at new 52-week highs. The bellwether 10-year yield briefly touched 5.35% this morning, the highest level since 2002. That means 30-year fixed mortgage rates will probably give back yesterday’s gains and possibly more. items.title: Mortgage Rates Finally Fall, But Not By Much
items.author: Colin Robertson
items.content: It’s been tough sledding for mortgage rates since early March. And especially rough over the past month and change, with very few down days.
